findings.summary: The new check is the first refusing check with no line in the reader's rules, so the reader learns the rule only after a refusal, at the cost of one re-read.
findings.evidence: briefs.rs:4400 says 'Each reading check in athena-core has its rule', and every current refusing check has a line in READING_RULES. With the reader set at 1998 of 2000 tokens, the plan relies on the refusal text alone. That is defensible, but the invariant that comment states becomes false without anyone saying so, and every reading that hits the rule pays a refusal plus a re-read. Fix: Have the doc comment and CHANGELOG item say plainly that the check has no reader rule line because of the budget, and that the first warning the reader gets is the refusal. Name the follow-up: make room in the reader set, or fold the boundary into the records-measures line (reader.rs:296) by saying 'run on real records via `status --snapshot`'. Optionally add the new check to the briefs.rs:4401 list as a known exception in a comment.

findings.summary: A stand-in place phrase anywhere in the criterion still exempts it, even when it does not say where the athena command runs.
findings.evidence: The rule is a stand-in word within three words after a place word, with no negation directly before it. So 'Run `athena status` on the real records and compare with a fixture', or '... then check the parser in a temp dir', is exempt even though the command still runs on the real queue. The plan lists only 'on a fixture, then on the real records' as a limit. Fix: Count a stand-in place phrase only when it is the first place phrase after the matched command and comes before the real-records phrase. Otherwise add 'compare with a fixture' to real_records_matching_limits as a flagged case, or name it in the doc comment's limits.

findings.summary: In corpus requests, a Depends line written as a bullet becomes a criterion and changes the bullet count.
findings.evidence: base_reading turns every request line that request_text_acceptance accepts ('- ', '* ', 'N. ') into a criterion. dependency_ids_in also accepts those prefixes (topics.rs:41-46). So a '1. Depends on: ...' or '- Depends on ...' line in a corpus request becomes an extra Content criterion, and bullets_expected and criteria[0] would not match. Fix: In step 5, say that the Depends line in corpus requests is a plain non-bullet line (for example 'Depends on: 20261030-070002-d103'). Test the bullet-prefixed Depends forms only in the unit test, where the reading is built separately from the request.
findings.location: Plan step 5 / Criterion 4 cases real-records-command-depends-on-d103 and -numbered; crates/athena-core/src/reading/topics.rs:266-282; refusal_corpus.rs:172-179

summary: Round 2. The one earlier major finding (round 1, finding 1: the refusal gave no repair the reader could use) is fixed. The error now offers three repairs, with `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>` as the reader's repair. Any criterion containing `--snapshot` is exempt. A unit test shows a records-measure reading that uses the plain command is refused by the new check, and the same reading rewritten as the error says passes both check_records_measure and the new check. The five round-1 minor findings are also fixed: step 7 now gives reasons for the three files left unchanged, the CHANGELOG item avoids other checks' `reading::check_` paths, the match is tighter (`cargo run` with athena-cli for the `-- <sub>` form, place-phrase stand-ins with negation, no `sample`), the sz3z case is labelled as guessed wording, and criterion 6 uses `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD`. I checked the plan's claims against the snapshot and they hold. The step position sits between check_scope_limit and check_boundary_and_repo_files (checks.rs:547-548). dependency_ids_in reads only 'Depends on' lines and the retry link (topics.rs:21-60). The evidence snapshot is written for every dispatched job (run/mod.rs:1170-1175) and the brief names `status --snapshot` (briefs.rs:669-671). Only `status` takes `--snapshot` (main.rs:431-434, 1116-1119). The corpus base reading has a capability (refusal_corpus.rs:198). d103 landed (HISTORY.txt:1104). I searched crates/ for criteria that run an athena command on real records: every hit uses `--snapshot` (refusal_corpus.rs:354, 441; run/tests.rs:5617; reading.rs:8412, 8424; surveys.rs:594), so the dependents list is complete. The remaining findings are minor: the new check has no line in the reader's rules, a stand-in phrase anywhere in a criterion still exempts it, and the corpus Depends cases need a non-bullet Depends line. None blocks the plan.
